title: Where should the photo booth go in a hotel ballroom?
summary: Give the booth a visible spot with room for a group to gather, a clear route past the line, and a place to collect prints. Agree on the spot with the banquet captain before the floor plan goes final.
alt: A group poses together at a Mango’s networking event
sections: Draw the line on the floor plan

On a plan of the room, draw three arrows. The first takes a guest from cocktail hour to the camera. The second takes them from the camera to their print. The third takes them back to their table. If the arrows cross the entrance, a server station or the route to the accessible seating, try the other side of the room.

For a Naples hotel reception with drinks in the foyer and dinner in the ballroom, choose the room where you want the booth operating during your booked hours. Ask whether the doors between the two spaces stay open. A booth behind a closed partition can look perfect on paper.
Send one setup note to both teams

Include the floor plan, event date, room name, loading entrance, permitted arrival time, outlet location and the name of the person opening the room. Ask Mango’s to confirm the footprint for your specific backdrop and keepsake station. Leave space to turn and pose together, including for guests using mobility aids.
For an outdoor terrace, get the indoor backup space in writing. Decide who calls the move and when, while the equipment can still be set up before guests arrive.
Give the coordinator a question they can forward

“Can our booth, pickup table and waiting guests fit here while your staff serve dinner? If we need another spot, which room and power outlet can we use?” Include a photo taken from the guest entrance. It shows a doorway or sightline that a floor plan can miss.

title: What does a photo booth cost in Southwest Florida?
summary: Mango’s three-hour packages are $550, $650 and $1,400, including travel across our Southwest Florida service area. The choice comes down to what you want guests to take home and how you want the booth to look.
alt: Floral wedding backdrop with a glowing Happily Ever After sign
sections: Start with what $550 covers

Luxury includes an attended open-air booth, unlimited on-site prints, one custom design, a standard backdrop, themed props and a private gallery. Choose either a 2×6 strip or a 4×6 photo. For a reception where the goal is a printed favor for guests, start your comparison here.
Decide what the extra $100 buys

Platinum is $650. It adds both print sizes, a second template, a deluxe backdrop, animated GIFs and a beauty filter. A planner who needs two designs for different sponsors has a concrete reason to consider that step up. If you simply want one logo on one print design, look at the included custom template first.
Compare the whole favor budget

Big Kahuna is $1,400 and brings together Platinum, a red carpet with stanchions, a premium custom backdrop, a live keychain or magnet station, a Mango Memory Frame and a decor enhancement. If you only want the favors, ask for a Luxury or Platinum quote with the station added. Compare those totals before deciding.

When requesting quotes, send every vendor the same date, venue and operating window. Ask which travel, prints, designs, attendant hours and optional upgrades appear in the total. These are Mango’s package prices. Your final quote should spell out the selections for your event.

title: Which three hours should we book for our wedding?
summary: Choose the stretch when guests can actually walk up, bring a friend and stay for a photo. Mark dinner service, speeches and room changes on the timeline before picking your start time.
alt: Guests gathered for a wedding photo with Mango’s
sections: Work backward from the pictures you want

If the photos you most want include grandparents and young children, ask when they expect to head home. If you want pictures of several friend groups together, look for the stretch when everyone is in the same room. A long guest list tells you less about this choice than the reception schedule.
Try two windows on the same timeline

Imagine cocktails at 5, dinner at 6 and dancing at 7. Booking 5–8 gives early arrivals a chance to visit and includes the first hour of dancing. Booking 7–10 keeps the booth available later but misses people who leave after dinner. These are sample windows you can place beside your own run sheet.

If cocktails and dancing happen in different rooms, mark the booth’s location next to each time. Ask your venue when guests can enter that room. Confirm any downtime or requested split schedule with your vendor before counting those minutes as available.
Plan for the rush after a toast

When everyone stands up at once, one large family may want a group photo followed by smaller combinations. Choose a spot with space to wait. Have your DJ tell guests where the booth is while it is open. If your ideal window still leaves someone out, ask about extra time before finalizing the run sheet.

title: Photo strips, magnets or keychains for your guests?
summary: Choose prints when you want a simple handoff, magnets for a photo guests can display, and keychains for a keepsake they can carry. Decide where the finished favor will go before choosing the design.
alt: Photo keychains from Mango’s Memory Station
sections: Match the format to the occasion

At a quinceañera, a 2×6 strip leaves room for a sequence of poses with friends. A 4×6 suits a larger portrait or a family group. For a company anniversary, think about whether the picture and company name will still read clearly on a small magnet or keychain. Ask to see the artwork at finished size.
Give pickup its own space

A live favor station adds a step after the photo. Put pickup where a guest can pause without standing in front of the next group. If the station is beside the exit, make sure guests can return for a favor without crossing the incoming line. Ask how to identify each finished item when several groups are waiting.
Choose a package after choosing the favor

Mango’s Luxury and Platinum packages include prints and can add a live keychain or magnet station. Big Kahuna includes a live station with a choice of keychains or magnets. When you ask for a quote, include your guest count, the type of keepsake and whether everyone is likely to arrive in one short break. Confirm quantities and pickup timing for that plan.

title: What should go in a branded photo booth brief?
summary: Give the vendor one page with the event goal, guest count, room schedule, approved artwork and the name of the person signing off. A clear brief helps marketing, the venue and the booth team plan the same experience.
alt: Mango’s booth at a networking event
sections: Name the job you want the booth to do

For an employee celebration, the priority might be getting departments into a group picture. For a sponsor reception, it might be giving guests a print they keep with the sponsor name on it. Write down one outcome the team can observe. A count of prints, for example, describes production. One guest may take several, so it cannot tell you how many individuals attended.
Proof the design in someone’s hand

Send the approved logo file, brand colors, required wording and artwork contact. Ask for a proof at the chosen print size. Check the sponsor name, date and faces at that size. A thin tagline that reads perfectly on a laptop may disappear on a strip. Agree on a final artwork deadline and who can approve changes.
Send this with your request for a quote

“We’re hosting [event] in [room and city] for [guest count]. Guests have [time window] between sessions. We want them to leave with [keepsake]. Our artwork approver is [contact]. Please confirm setup access, what’s included in the quote, and which activity counts you can provide afterward.”

If the team wants guests to share pictures, decide where to display the event handle and which photos you have permission to repost. Ask for marketing permission separately from photo delivery. That gives guests a clear choice and gives your team a clearer measure of interest.

title: How many guests can one photo booth serve?
summary: At Mango’s, a guest-count charge applies only to events with more than 50 guests. To plan booth time, also consider how many people want individual photos and when they’ll have a chance to take them.
alt: Four friends sharing one turn at the photo booth
sections: Does Mango’s charge more for over 50 guests?

Yes. Our three-hour packages start at $550 for Luxury, $650 for Platinum and $1,400 for Big Kahuna. For events with more than 50 guests, the additional charge depends on your guest count. Send us your expected headcount and preferred package so we can quote the total.

For example, if you expect 80 people at your reception, use 80 when requesting pricing. For planning the booth schedule, it also helps to know whether you expect guests to pose in couples, families or individual portraits.
Does a small party need a minimum number of guests?

For a dinner with 25 guests, start with the pictures people would want. A family portrait with three generations, cousins together and a print for each household can make the booth worthwhile even if it sits quiet between groups. If everyone wants just one group picture, ask whether your event photographer can cover it before you budget for a separate booth.
How to estimate turns for 120 guests

A turn is one group’s visit to the camera. Suppose 90 of your 120 wedding guests want a photo and they come in groups averaging three. That’s about 30 turns. If 10 groups come back for another combination, plan for 40 turns. Spread over two open hours, that calls for 20 turns per hour. Squeeze those same 40 turns into a half-hour cocktail reception and the required pace rises to 80 per hour.

These are example schedules. For your own estimate, divide the number of people who want a photo by the typical group size, round up, then add repeat turns. Divide by the time guests can actually use the booth. If the goal is a separate portrait for every attendee, count one turn per person.
What does a vendor’s hourly estimate count?

Mid America Photo Booth reports averaging 45–50 sessions per hour on its setup. Dan’s Camera City suggests planning for about 50 guests per hour and says the mix of solo guests, couples and groups affects that figure. The units matter. Four friends posing together can mean one session, four people photographed and several print copies.

Ask your operator how long it takes from one group stepping in to the next group being ready. Include the pose sequence, extra copies and where guests collect their prints. Use a pace measured with a setup like yours, and leave room for retakes and families getting settled.
When would a second booth help?

If guests can drift over throughout the evening, opening earlier or inviting tables in waves may give everyone time. If all attendees leave the same Naples hotel meeting at once and must return in 30 minutes, an extra hour after the meeting won’t help that break. Ask about a second camera station if posing is the slow step. If people are waiting for magnets while the camera sits free, a separate pickup spot addresses that line.

When you contact Mango’s, send your expected headcount, whether people will pose together or individually, and the length of your busiest break. Tell us if every guest needs a particular photo or favor. Those details let us discuss a setup and schedule that fit your event.
